name: Horologium
introduction: is the Pendulum Clock, introduced by Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in the 1750s to honor Christiaan Huygens’s invention. It is a faint, winding line of stars in the southern sky near Achernar.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Horologium includes one of the Sun’s nearest neighbors, [GJ 1061](id:10pc-0045), a red dwarf 12 light-years away with three small planets, one of which lies in its habitable zone.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alpha Horologii](hip:19747), the brightest star, is an orange giant about 120 light-years away. Iota Horologii, nearby, is a Sun-like star with a giant planet that likely formed in the same cloud as the Hyades.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Far beyond the stars lies the Horologium Supercluster, one of the largest structures in the nearby universe. The globular cluster NGC 1261 and many faint galaxies also lie in this direction.
